fieldMarks: Charcoal above and white below, sharply two-toned in summer with more white on the face in winter
Similar Thick-billed Murre is very close; compare to loons
behavior: Purring or murmuring call (hence the name), plus a guttural croak and higher bleat
Forages swimming underwater, diving over 150 ft; eats herring, cod, capelin, sand lance and other fish, plus crustaceans, worms and squid
Nests on cliff ledges and flat bare rock atop sea stacks; permanent resident in many areas but must leave northern western-Alaska colonies when waters freeze
habitat: Ocean and large bays, favoring cool waters over the continental shelf, offshore and rather near the coast; tends to avoid pack ice.
range: Breeds along North Pacific coasts from the Bering Strait south to central California and the North Atlantic from western Greenland and Iceland south to Newfoundland; some birds reach New England waters and southern California in winter.

lookalikes.name: Thick-billed murre
lookalikes.howToTell: Slightly thicker bill with a white mark at the gape, blacker back, and often more black on the face in winter.
